voice.name: en-GB-SoniaNeural
voice.prosody: Getting lost here is part of the plan. It all began with a bedesten built in the time of Mehmed the Conqueror: a thick-walled, lockable hall where valuable goods were traded. Over time streets, inns and domes grew around it, until the bazaar became a small city of its own. Today there are about 4,000 shops. Each street used to belong to one trade, such as jewellers, carpet sellers or hat makers, and many of those names are still on the signs. On its busiest days, close to half a million people are said to pass through. Don't stay on the main street. Slip through the side gates into the old inns, where silversmiths and craftsmen still work at their benches. If a shop offers you tea, it's polite to accept, and you don't have to buy anything. The old inns around the bazaar are part of it too. A han was a courtyard building where merchants both stayed and stored their goods. A glance into the courtyard of a place like Zincirli Han is like seeing the real heart of the bazaar.
